note.fact: For the supplied prime p and any nonzero rational q, there exist d∈Z and u∈Q with q=p^d u such that u and u^(-1) both belong to R={a/b:p does not divide b}.

grounds.reason: This is the exact definition of R.
F002 ensures the rational coefficients for nonzero generators are nonzero.
S003 explicitly removes powers of p from numerator and denominator.

note.justification: Represent q=A/B with nonzero integers A,B. Successively divide A and B by p while divisible. The positive absolute value strictly decreases at each division, so each process terminates: A=p^α A_0 and B=p^β B_0 for α,β≥0 with p dividing neither A_0 nor B_0. Put d=α−β and u=A_0/B_0. Both u and its inverse have denominators not divisible by p and thus lie in R. The exponent is well defined: two such decompositions with different exponents would, after clearing denominators prime to p, force p to divide a product of integers none divisible by p, contradicting primality.
